artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.

The SJC denied the specifications, holding that BCO 31-2 gives the investigating court great discretion over procedure and timing and that the record did not show clear error; related complainants lacked standing.

artifacts.title: Chastain v. Heritage
artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.title: Thornton v. Westminster Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE James Thornton complained that Westminster Presbytery erred by declining to place a valid call from Memorial PCA into his hands and simultaneously invoking BCO 34-10 to begin divestiture proceedings. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the administrative remedy of BCO 34-10 cannot be invoked when a call is already in the presbytery's possession, and that presbytery's refusal lacked objective, justifiable grounds required for appellate review.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Anthony Dallison appealed his deposition from the office of Teaching Elder by North Florida Presbytery, arguing that presbytery lacked authority to increase his censure from indefinite suspension to deposition without conducting a new trial. The SJC affirmed presbytery's decision, holding that where a teaching elder has confessed guilt under BCO 38-1, presbytery may impose additional censure based on evidence of impenitence without initiating new charges, and such disciplinary discretion is within presbytery's constitutional authority.
